system_overview: This specification models the N-Queens problem using PlusCal, an algorithmic language that translates to TLA+. It implements the same iterative backtracking algorithm as the plain TLA+ version: given an N-by-N chessboard, find all arrangements of N queens such that no two queens threaten each other (no shared row, column, or diagonal). The PlusCal version makes the sequential control flow explicit through a labeled while loop.
actors_and_components: The system consists of a single solver that iteratively processes partial queen placements. The solver uses a loop that repeatedly selects a partial placement, computes all valid single-row extensions, and either records complete solutions or queues new partial placements for further processing.
state_variables: The system tracks three pieces of state: (1) a set of partial placements awaiting processing, where each partial placement is an ordered list of column positions shorter than the board size, (2) a set of completed solutions found so far, where each is a complete list of column positions of length N, and (3) a program counter that tracks whether the algorithm is still iterating or has finished.
initial_state: The work set contains a single empty placement (no queens placed). The result set is empty. The program counter indicates the algorithm is at the beginning of its main loop.
actions: While the work set is non-empty, the solver selects any partial placement, determines the next row to fill, and computes all columns where a new queen can be placed without conflicting with previously placed queens. A conflict means two queens share the same column or the same diagonal. Each valid extension is constructed by appending the chosen column to the partial placement. If this completes all N rows, the extension goes into the result set; otherwise it goes into the work set. The selected partial placement is removed from the work set. When the work set is empty, the algorithm transitions to a done state and permits only stuttering steps.
safety_properties: The result set contains only valid solutions: no completed placement has two queens that attack each other. When the algorithm terminates, the result set contains every possible valid placement.
liveness_properties: The algorithm eventually terminates: the program counter eventually reaches the done state, meaning all partial placements have been fully explored.
model_bounds: The board size N is a constant positive natural number. For model checking, N must be set to a specific finite value.
additional_assumptions: The PlusCal translation includes an explicit termination-detecting step that allows infinite stuttering once the algorithm completes, preventing the model checker from reporting deadlock. A separate liveness condition can be added via weak fairness on the main loop action to guarantee termination.
